request:
Crisis is an in-house Mandarin Chinese psychological-support hotline dataset comprising 154 recordings (approximately 100 hours in total; mean duration 39.49 minutes). 
The study was conducted at the Beijing Psychological Support Hotline which provides services to callers from around China, three-fourths of whom live outside of the Beijing Municipality. Hotline operators are full-time employees with a psychology or psychiatry background who receive at least 3 months full-time training in the provision of hotline services before independently taking calls.
Recordings were independently annotated by two clinical experts into three crisis levels: no crisis (55 participants), low crisis (42), and medium-to-high crisis (57). Conversations cover a broad range of personal issues, including depression, anxiety, relationship stress and suicidal ideation, and may contain privacy-sensitive information such as names, locations and phone numbers.
The study was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Beijing Huilongguan Hospital (2014-106, 2024-76). Before callers were connected to a hotline operator, they were informed by a voice message that all calls of the hotline would be tape-recorded and that data utilised for research purposes would be analysed anonymously.  Keep the spoken content and evaluate all methods to summarize what works for this task.
